forces.title: Gaming surpasses film, shifts M&E market dominance
forces.description: The online gaming segment in India grew significantly by 22% in 2023, becoming the fourth-largest segment of the Media & Entertainment (M&E) sector. This growth led to online gaming displacing 'filmed entertainment' from its previous position. This indicates a structural shift in consumer engagement and spending priorities towards interactive digital entertainment, potentially diverting audience and investment away from traditional film.
forces.source_title: Media and Entertainment Industry In India

forces.title: Film's M&E market share shrinking amidst digital growth
forces.description: Filmed entertainment's share of the overall Media & Entertainment sector is projected to decrease from 7.83% in 2026 to 7.66% in 2028. This trend, despite the overall M&E sector growing, signifies that film is expanding at a slower pace compared to other segments like digital media (13.5% CAGR), animation & VFX (17.5% CAGR), and online gaming (20.7% CAGR), which are identified as the fastest-growing segments. This suggests a long-term re-allocation of consumer attention and industry investment.
forces.source_title: Media and Entertainment Industry In India

forces.title: Government policy to boost Animation, VFX, Gaming, Comics
forces.description: The Indian government, through the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting, is actively working on an Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming, and Comic (AVGC) policy and an AVGC Mission. This initiative aims to support and develop these creative segments, which include critical components like VFX that are integral to modern film production. This policy support could foster talent, technology, and infrastructure, benefiting the film industry's technical aspects.
forces.source_title: Media and Entertainment Industry In India

forces.title: India eyes significant share of global VFX market
forces.description: India has a strong potential to capture approximately 5% of the US$40 billion global Animation and Visual Effects (VFX) market. This segment is forecast to achieve annual growth of 25-30% and is expected to create over 1.6 lakh new jobs annually. Such robust growth in VFX directly supports film production capabilities, potentially making India a hub for post-production and special effects for global and domestic films, driving demand for these specialized services.
forces.source_title: Media and Entertainment Industry In India

viewpoints.title: Filmed entertainment faces relative decline, losing M&E market share to digital segments
viewpoints.description: The IBEF report indicates a cautious outlook for filmed entertainment, as it was displaced by online gaming as the fourth-largest M&E segment in 2023. Projections show its share of the total M&E market decreasing from 7.83% in 2026 to 7.66% in 2028. This suggests a slower growth trajectory for film compared to digital media, animation & VFX, and online gaming, which are highlighted as fastest-growing segments. This shift reflects evolving consumer preferences and industry dynamics favoring digital consumption.
viewpoints.source_title: Media and Entertainment Industry In India
